about: Scenes for the animated video of Overcoming Common Pitfalls in Early Stage Product Development for Healthcare SaaS. Each scene starts at a phrase in the narration ("at"); keys ending in At name phrases that trigger a move inside the scene. Chapter cards (one per pitfall) are added by render.mjs.

scenes.at: Most healthcare startups don't fail on the idea
scenes.text: Most healthcare startups don't fail on the idea. They fail on assumptions that don't hold up in real healthcare environments.

scenes.at: The good news is that many of the most common mistakes are avoidable
scenes.label: The good news
scenes.text: Know where healthcare SaaS tends to go wrong, and decide better from the start.

scenes.at: One of the biggest mistakes early stage healthcare SaaS startups make
scenes.label: Pitfall 1: the founder's vision, not the user's workflow
cards: Clinicians work under time pressure, rules and established processes.
A problem can look simple and still not fit how the work is done.
End users, economic buyers, operators. Real constraints, real decisions.

scenes.at: Avoiding this pitfall requires more than
Healthcare startups often feel pressure to appear enterprise ready
scenes.label: Pitfall 2: too much, too early
items: one painful problem, one user group
scenes.note: In early-stage product development, focus is a strategic advantage.

scenes.at: The strongest healthcare SaaS products usually begin
scenes.label: Credibility
scenes.text: Solve one painful problem for one clearly defined user group, then expand.

scenes.at: In healthcare, standalone software often struggles
scenes.label: Pitfall 3: what customers already run
cards: The tools the front desk lives in.

scenes.at: treat integration as part of the product strategy
scenes.label: Integration is product strategy
items: about what you can support today

scenes.at: In healthcare, trust is not a finishing layer
scenes.label: Pitfall 4: security and compliance later
scenes.text: Not a finishing layer added after the product works. HIPAA, data governance, auditability, security.

scenes.at: build with compliance-aware habits from day one
scenes.label: Compliance-aware habits from day one

scenes.at: In healthcare organizations, the person who loves a product
scenes.label: Pitfall 5: who shapes the purchase decision
items: End user: loves the time saved
Department leaders: want proof it scales

scenes.at: Successful teams map the full buying journey early
scenes.label: Map the buying journey early

scenes.at: Because budgets are tight and adoption can be slow
scenes.label: Pitfall 6: value that's hard to see
scenes.text: If the impact is vague or hard to measure, implementation is hard to justify.

scenes.at: Define success metrics early
scenes.label: Metrics a buyer can take to the budget meeting

scenes.at: Many healthcare SaaS startups treat pilots
scenes.label: Pitfall 7: pilots that never decide

scenes.at: Design pilots with discipline instead
scenes.label: Design pilots with discipline
items: goals, users, duration, metrics and decision points
so the customer sees value quickly
does it work here, and does it merit broader adoption?
itemAt: Make the pilot answer one specific question

scenes.at: Reduce this risk by involving domain expertise
scenes.label: Involve domain expertise early and continuously
scenes.text: Clinical advisors, provider operators, reimbursement experts, compliance consultants, healthcare product leaders.

scenes.at: That is why implementation is a core product concern
scenes.label: Pitfall 9: implementation is product design

scenes.label: How resilient healthcare SaaS companies grow
